patterns: Monthly roundups of made things: Pınar's 'what I drew in October' did ~15k views and 1,482 likes on about 1k followers. A month-end look at handmade work travels far past an account's size. Brand angle: ask people what they made by hand this month.

Relatable one-liner plus image: 'How it feels to do anything as a neurodivergent person' hit ~322k views and 2,361 saves from a 301-follower account. Naming a feeling exactly, with no advice attached, is what got shared.
Save-worthy lists: the Japan stationery shop guide (~43k views, 596 saves) was saved more than liked. Practical, specific, place-named lists earn saves on her topic.

Going back to paper: a cartoonist returning to pen and ink, 'dropping the iPad for the fountain pen', and a week with a fountain pen writing 'more than in the past 4 months' all showed up in one day. Small accounts, real sentiment, few replies yet.

Open questions pull replies: 'What are you all currently reading?' got 82 replies (~12.8k views), and the generic version on small accounts gets almost nothing. The question works when the account already has readers.
Skip: Yongfook's 'it's research, not coding' (~9k, 71 replies) is AI tooling with low brand fit, and SRKDAN's 'every AI-built site looks the same' is a product promo.

reply_ideas.description: cartoonist Mary Goglia going back to pen and ink on paper for her comic after cleaning up her art area
reply_ideas.reply_text: Funny how a clean desk changes what you want to make. Once there's room for an ink bottle, the screen starts to feel like the long way around. Are you lettering the balloons by hand too, or keeping that part digital?

reply_ideas.description: ADHD as an endless loop of needing to do another thing first
reply_ideas.reply_text: The part that gets me is that every step makes sense on its own, so it never feels like you've wandered off until you're standing in the wrong room holding the 3rd thing. Has writing the 1st thing on paper ever helped you, or does the note just turn into another thing?

reply_ideas.description: solo Shopify app founder whose second review held a release even after 43 automated checks
reply_ideas.reply_text: I'm building my Shopify shop right now, so I'm curious what the second review caught that 43 checks didn't. Was it something a person only notices by actually using it, like how a page feels on a phone?

bip_draft:
Building Calmly Crashing mostly by myself means every page on the site is one I argued with first.

The shop is close. I'm still saying no to anything I wouldn't buy for myself.

#buildinpublic
video_tip: 15 seconds, no face. A cluttered desk gets cleared with one arm on textured cream paper. An ink bottle is set down, a fountain pen is uncapped, and the nib draws one slow line. Desk and nib sounds only, no music. End on a card that reads 'What did you make by hand in October?' Pairs with the made-in-October post.

x_posts.title: What a notebook needs
x_posts.text:
A good notebook doesn't need to be expensive.

It needs paper that doesn't bleed while the ink is wet and a binding that stays open when you're tired. Everything past that is taste.
